label: Channel manager API
purpose: Requests that hotels' channel managers send to the Channel Manager API to push rate updates and hotel information into GlobalTravelEngine. Includes the hotels and contracts the requests carry, response times, errors and warnings.
grain: Aggregated channel manager API requests per day, hour, API user, channel manager, integration type, request type, error, warning and response-time band.
use_for: channel manager requests by day, hour, channel manager or API user
channel manager response times (average and by time band)
hotels and contracts carried by channel manager requests
not_for: number of rate changes or rate updates (Statistics Rate Changes Channel Manager API)
the rates or prices themselves (not stored)
supplier or client API traffic (Statistics Hotel Supplier, Statistics Hotel Client)
anything older than about one year

coverage.note: Rolling window of about one year: the oldest day drops off every day (on 2026-10-16 the Calendar started around 2025-10-17), so October 2025 is partial and last-year comparisons are not possible. The oldest day still loaded (about 0.66 million requests) has no 'Calendar' date: all-time totals and 'Date'[Date] include it, and monthly figures from 'Calendar' do not.

dates.label: Request date
dates.meaning: Day the request was received (the cube's main date, with year, quarter, month and week attributes).

dates.label: Request date (plain table)
dates.meaning: The same request date in a plain date table with no attributes. It matches 'Calendar'[Date] month by month, except that it also holds the oldest loaded day (October 2025), which 'Calendar' lacks.

measures.name: [Requests]
measures.label: Channel manager requests
measures.definition: Number of API requests received from channel managers (successful or not).
measures.notes: Main measure. 199.7 million all-time, 188.9 million in the last 12 months.

measures.name: [Hotels]
measures.label: Hotels in requests
measures.definition: Hotels carried by the requests, added up per request: a hotel sent in 100 requests counts 100 times. It is not a number of distinct hotels.

measures.name: [Contracts]
measures.label: Contracts in requests
measures.definition: Hotel contracts carried by the requests, added up per request (not distinct contracts).

measures.name: [Bookings]
measures.label: Bookings in requests
measures.definition: Bookings carried or returned by channel manager requests. The exact meaning is not confirmed.
measures.notes: About 93,000 all-time against about 200 million requests, although 'Get bookings' requests have no data. Never use it for "bookings" questions (see review).

measures.name: [Total Time]
measures.label: Total response time
measures.definition: Sum of response times of the requests, in milliseconds.
measures.hidden_reason: helper of [AVG Time] (sum of response times in milliseconds)

measures.name: [AVG Time]
measures.label: Average response time
measures.definition: Average response time per request ([Total Time] ÷ [Requests]), in milliseconds.
measures.notes: About 218 ms all-time. The unit is inferred from the 'Range Times' bands (0 - 100, 100 - 200 ...), where most requests fall.

measures.name: [AVG Bookings]
measures.label: Bookings per request
measures.notes: About 0.0005: it shows 0.00 at this format. Same open question as [Bookings].

breakdowns.label: Request type
breakdowns.meaning: Kind of request. Almost all are 'Update rates'; 'Hotel information' is the only other type with data.

breakdowns.label: Channel manager
breakdowns.meaning: Channel manager company that sent the request. One company sends about 98% of the traffic.

breakdowns.label: Integration type
breakdowns.meaning: Integration protocol or connector used. Two types have data; one channel manager's V2 connector carries almost everything.

breakdowns.label: API user
breakdowns.meaning: API login of the hotel or hotel chain sending the requests.

breakdowns.label: Error
breakdowns.meaning: Error returned to the request; 'Correct' means no error.
sample_values: Login fails - Invalid user or password

breakdowns.label: Error code
breakdowns.meaning: Technical code of the error; 'Correct' means no error.

breakdowns.label: Warning
breakdowns.meaning: Warning returned with the request; 'Correct' means no warning. 'Incorrect Additional Price' is about 30% of the hotel volume.
sample_values: Allotment can not be modified because the used allotment is higher than the base-extra

breakdowns.label: Weekday
breakdowns.meaning: Day of the week (Monday to Sunday).

breakdowns.label: Hour of day
breakdowns.meaning: Hour the request was received, "00" to "23".

named_filters.name: rate update requests
named_filters.meaning: Requests that push rate updates (API calls, not the number of rate changes they carry).

named_filters.name: incorrect additional price warnings
named_filters.meaning: Requests that got the 'Incorrect Additional Price' warning.

named_filters.name: slow channel manager requests
named_filters.meaning: Requests that took more than 1 second, or timed out.

rules: [Requests] counts API calls. "Rate changes" and "rate updates" are counted by [Changes] in Statistics Rate Changes Channel Manager API; the 'rate update requests' filter here counts the calls that carried them.
[Hotels], [Contracts] and [Bookings] add up per request, so a hotel counts once for every request. Never present them as a number of distinct hotels, contracts or bookings.
[AVG Time], [AVG Hotels], [AVG Contracts] and [AVG Bookings] are averages per request: never add them across rows. [AVG Time] is in milliseconds.
Error share = [Requests] with Error Type Code other than 'Correct' ÷ all [Requests]. Warning share works the same way with Warning Type Code.
About one year of data (rolling window). Last-year comparisons are not possible and October 2025 is partial.
'IPs'[IP] is almost entirely 'Unknown': do not break down by IP.
Get rates, Get bookings, Offers and Others requests have no data.

review.question: Which date should plain questions use: 'Calendar'[Date] or 'Date'[Date]?
review.why: Both are the request date and match month by month. 'Calendar' has the month, week and quarter attributes used for grouping; it misses only the oldest loaded day (about 0.66 million requests, October 2025).

review.question: What do [Bookings] and [AVG Bookings] count in channel manager requests, and should they be shown at all?
options: Keep them active, only for "bookings in channel manager requests"
review.proposed: Keep them active, only for "bookings in channel manager requests"
review.why: They have data (about 93,000 in all), but 'Get bookings' requests show none, so their meaning is unclear. They must never answer plain "bookings" questions.

review.question: "How many hotels use channel managers": hotel occurrences in requests, or distinct hotels?
options: Distinct hotels: count of 'Hotels'[Hotel] with [Changes] in Statistics Rate Changes Channel Manager API
review.proposed: Distinct hotels: count of 'Hotels'[Hotel] with [Changes] in Statistics Rate Changes Channel Manager API
review.why: [Hotels] counts a hotel once for every request (about 196 million all-time), so it measures volume, not how many hotels.
